title: Dirty Data Injection (DIRTY)
summary: Echoes a price series with regular gaps cut into it, so you can see how other studies cope with missing bars.
descriptionHtml:
Dirty Data Injection is a test tool rather than a market study. It copies the chosen source series bar for bar, but blanks it on a fixed schedule: the very first bar is always empty, and after that the first few bars of every cycle are left empty too.

The cycle length is the NA Injection Interval and the number of blank bars at the start of each cycle is the NA Gap Size. A bar is blank when its position in the run, divided by the interval, leaves a remainder smaller than the gap size. With the defaults of 10 and 5, bars 0 to 4 are blank, bars 5 to 9 carry the source, bars 10 to 14 are blank again, and so on.

Nothing is smoothed or averaged. Every value that is drawn is exactly the source value on that bar.
howToReadHtml:
Read it as a picture of a broken data feed. The line is the source where data is present and a gap where it has been removed, so it shows at a glance which bars an indicator would have to handle without a value.

It carries no trading signal. Its use is in building and checking other scripts: feed the same gap pattern into a calculation and confirm that its warmup, its running sums and its markers behave sensibly when bars are missing, rather than treating a gap as zero.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series that is copied onto the chart where it is not blanked.

settings.label: NA Injection Interval
settings.html: The length of one cycle in bars. A larger value spaces the gaps further apart.

settings.label: NA Gap Size
settings.html: How many bars at the start of each cycle are left empty. A value equal to or above the interval blanks every bar.

faq.q: Why is the first bar always empty?
faq.html: The first bar is blanked unconditionally, in addition to the gap at the start of every cycle, so every run begins with a missing value.

faq.q: Is this meant to be traded?
faq.html: No. It reproduces the source with holes in it. Its only job is to give other calculations a series with known gaps to test against.

faq.q: What happens if the gap size is larger than the interval?
faq.html: Every bar falls inside a gap, so nothing is drawn at all.

related.title: Huber Loss (HUBER)
related.summary: The average Huber penalty of the gap between price and its own exponential average: squared for small gaps, linear for large ones.

related.title: Log-Cosh Loss
related.summary: A rolling average of log(cosh(actual minus predicted)), an error measure that acts squared for small misses and linear for large ones.

related.title: Mean Arctangent Absolute Percentage Error
related.summary: A rolling average of the arctangent of the absolute percentage error between two series, bounded between zero and pi/2.
